## Teaching points

1. Biphasic (type A) or deeply inverted (type B) T waves in V2–V4, recorded while pain-free, mark critical proximal LAD stenosis and a high risk of extensive anterior infarction.
2. Young age, pleuritic or non-exertional pain and odd relieving factors do not outweigh an ischemic ECG; interpret the tracing on its own merits.
3. Pericarditis causes diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression; its T waves invert only after the ST segments normalize, not as a pain-free biphasic pattern.
4. Troponin may be normal or elevated in Wellens syndrome; most cases present as NSTEMI.
5. Treat as high-risk NSTE-ACS: antithrombotic therapy and early invasive angiography; stress testing can provoke infarction.
